newsitem.title: GERMANY: North German firm eyes Poland sugar investments.
newsitem.headline: North German firm eyes Poland sugar investments.

text.p: Zuckerverbund North (ZVN) is studying opportunities in the Polish sugar industry, where plants are coming up for privatisation, a spokesman for the north German group said.
"It is definitely the most attractive market in eastern Europe -- with 40 million inhabitants and significant growth chances in sugar consumption," he said.
"Poland also has a long tradition of sugar production and suitable plant and machinery manufacturers."
Company statements on release of 1996/97 (Feb/March) figures listed among the projects under consideration the Opalenica plant, where ZVN is seeking a stake.
ZVN is also among the bidders for the Glinojeck refinery and is studying a number of other plants in the Bydogoscz area.
Apart from Poland, ZVN also views companies in Hungary, the Czech republic and Slovenia as potential partners.
But the spokesman said nothing was likely to be decided before autumn elections in Poland.
German investment interest was a sensitive issue in view of the two countries' history.
This was helping to push potential sales prices higher.
ZVN had been looking into Poland's 70 refineries for the last two years and it was not the only interested party.
Cologne-based Pfeiffer & Langen as well as Mannheim-based Suedzucker AG were also involved.
Suedzucker is leading in European sugar processing with Franco-Italian Eridania Beghin-Say.
ZVN aims to lead a merger of four northern German sugar processing firms into a new ZVN AG by the autumn, creating Europe's third largest sugar group with two billion marks of annual turnover.
ZVN's latest annual figures showed it produced 762,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996/97 (Feb/March), 64,000 tonnes more than a year earlier.
The beet volume processed, at 4.65 million tonnes, was down by 2.3 percent from 1995/96.
Profits rose to 7.2 million marks from 5.4 million on turnover of 913 million (908 million).
